request: We should know which of our contacts are most influential so we can prioritize them.
pre_mortem: A year after launch, the influence scoring feature inadvertently caused a diplomatic incident. An executive received an alert about a high-influence contact from a country where our organization has sensitive engagements. This alert was based on incorrect influence scores that were assigned without adequate vetting, leading to actions that were deemed inappropriate in that diplomatic context, resulting in a public relations crisis and a reassessment of our engagement strategy in that region.

How will data used to calculate influence scores be gathered and validated across different regions?

proposals.summary: This release will introduce a feature to categorize and rank contacts based on their level of influence within government counterparts. It will provide regional coordinators and project managers with the ability to view and prioritize contacts based on defined influence criteria.

core_commitments.text: Categorize contacts by influence level based on specific criteria.
Provide a searchable and filterable interface for users to prioritize contacts.

in_scope.text: Define 'influence' based on factors such as position, seniority, and past engagement outcomes.
Allow users to assign an 'influence score' to each contact, ranging from 1 (low influence) to 5 (high influence).
Develop a dashboard for regional coordinators and project managers to view and filter contacts by influence level.
Ensure that the feature respects existing privacy and data sensitivity guidelines.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not incorporate machine learning or AI to auto-generate influence scores.
The release will not include historical data analysis of engagement outcomes to influence future scoring.
This release will not change the existing user privacy settings or access controls.

assumptions.text: Assuming that users have access to sufficient data regarding contacts' position and engagement within their respective ministries, which is necessary for influence scoring.
Assuming that the influence scoring method can be standardized across different countries and contexts.
Assuming that there will be no legal barriers preventing the internal categorization of contacts based on their influence.

definitions.text: 'Influential contact' means a contact within a government counterpart who holds substantial sway over decision-making processes.
